projectCharter.projectBackground: A new passenger elevator is planned for a commercial complex at Hinjewadi, Pune.
projectCharter.engineeringContext: Students act as mechanical design engineers reviewing suspension cable selection before procurement.
objectives: Understand the elevator suspension cable safety problem.
Apply machine element design reasoning to load distribution and material selection.
Prepare an engineering decision with professional justification based on standard safety codes.
projectCharter.professionalResponsibility: Students must prioritize safety, reliability, and accountable engineering documentation.
projectCharter.safetyConsiderations: Elevator suspension systems are safety-critical. According to ASME A17.1 / EN 81, suspension ropes must have a minimum Factor of Safety of 10 for passenger elevators.
projectCharter.acceptanceCriteria: The project is complete when all activities are attempted, calculations are documented, and the final decision is justified against the required standard.

cards.title: Client
cards.body: ABC Commercial Complex Pvt Ltd, Hinjewadi, Pune.

cards.title: Project Background
cards.body: The client is installing a passenger elevator and requires an independent academic engineering review of selected suspension cables before procurement.

cards.title: Engineering Context
cards.body: You are a mechanical design engineer evaluating whether the suspension cable choice and load distribution appear technically reasonable against safety standards.

cards.title: Objectives
items: Connect cable safety to Design of Machine Elements.

cards.title: Safety Standards
cards.body: Elevator suspension cables are safety-critical. According to standards like ASME A17.1, passenger elevator suspension ropes must have a minimum Factor of Safety of 10.

cards.title: Acceptance Criteria
cards.body: Continue only after you understand the client problem, safety context, deliverables, and professional responsibility.

identify-components.title: Identify the Components of a Traction Elevator System
identify-components.image: ./Engineering Assets Library/EA-01 Traction Elevator System/Student Version/EA-01_Student_v1.0.png
identify-components.description: Student version of the traction elevator system engineering asset with numbered callouts 1-20.

labels.feedback: The electric motor provides rotational input for the traction drive.
The drive sheave transmits traction to the suspension ropes.
The suspension wire ropes carry the elevator car and counterweight.
The elevator car carries passengers between floor levels.
The car frame supports and guides the elevator car assembly.
The counterweight balances part of the car load.
Car guide rails constrain elevator car motion.
Counterweight guide rails constrain counterweight motion.
The deflector sheave guides the rope path.
The machine beam supports machinery loads.
The shaft is the vertical space in which the elevator system operates.
The pit is the lower space beneath the lowest landing.
The pit buffer absorbs impact at the bottom limit of travel.
Top clearance is the space above the car at upper travel.
Landing doors separate each floor from the elevator shaft.
Floor levels indicate the building landings served by the elevator.
The passenger represents the live load carried by the elevator car.
The rope path shows how the suspension ropes are routed.
The elevator motion arrow indicates car travel direction.
The rope movement arrow indicates rope travel over the sheaves.

working-principle.title: Working Principle of Traction Elevator
working-principle.prompt: Explain how a traction elevator works. Include the role of the motor, traction sheave, ropes, counterweight, guide rails, elevator car, controller, and safety gear.

mcq.question: Which component directly provides traction to move the suspension ropes?

engineering-model.title: Engineering Model
engineering-model.prompt: Explain the load path transferring the passenger load to the suspension system.

options: Weight -> Load Distribution -> Tension in Rope
Tension in Rope -> Load Distribution -> Weight
Load Distribution -> Weight -> Tension in Rope

design-requirements.title: Design Requirements & Safety Standards
given: Identify the core requirements and standards from the problem statement.
design-requirements.expectedProcess: Students must explicitly state the numerical requirements and the standard Factor of Safety constraint before starting calculations.

material-selection.title: Material Selection
material-selection.prompt: Compare the given candidate materials and recommend the most suitable suspension cable material for this application.

options.title: Mild Steel (Syt = 250 MPa)
options.note: Economical and easy to process but not preferred for high-strength suspension cables.

options.title: High Carbon Steel (Syt = 800 MPa)
options.note: High tensile strength and commonly used in steel wire rope applications.

options.title: Stainless Steel (Syt = 500 MPa)
options.note: Corrosion resistant but grade, cost, and strength must be verified.

options.title: Synthetic Rope (Syt = N/A)
options.note: Lightweight and specialized; requires compatibility, certification, and long-term performance review.

steps.title: Step 1: Passenger Mass
steps.label: Passenger Mass (kg)
steps.formula: Number of passengers × Weight per passenger

steps.title: Step 4: Load on One Rope
steps.label: Load on One Rope (N)
steps.formula: Total Load ÷ Number of suspension ropes

steps.title: Step 5: Required Breaking Load
steps.label: Required Breaking Load (N)
steps.formula: Load on One Rope × Factor of Safety

steps.title: Step 7: Standard Rope Diameter
steps.label: Selection of the nearest higher standard rope diameter (mm)
steps.feedback: Correct. Using a standard 10mm or 12mm rope provides a safe margin.

steps.title: Step 8: Actual Tensile Stress
steps.label: Actual Stress (MPa)
steps.formula: Load on One Rope / (0.38 × d²). Note: 0.38 d² is the effective metallic cross-sectional area for a standard wire rope as per Bhandari.
steps.feedback: Correct. Using Load on One Rope / (0.38 × d²).

steps.title: Step 9: Actual Factor of Safety
steps.label: Actual Factor of Safety
steps.feedback: Correct. Syt (800 MPa for high carbon steel) / Actual Stress.

steps.title: Step 10: Engineering Reflection
steps.label: Why do actual elevators often use a larger standard rope?
steps.formula: Discuss: Dynamic loading, Bending over sheaves, Wear, Shock loading, Unequal load distribution
steps.feedback: Excellent reasoning. Safety factors cover these complex dynamic scenarios.

engineering-decision.title: Engineering Decision
engineering-decision.prompt: Compare your calculated Required Rope Diameter against the proposed Selected Standard Diameter (12 mm). Decide whether the current suspension cable design should be approved for procurement. Provide engineering justification.
